decisions.reason: Piqué builds on existing upholstery weaving knowledge and remains in the collection, so the firm can interpret early results and improve it despite reduced web prominence.
Its limited website presence and weaker fit with the firm’s core woven upholstery and curtain expertise reduce the firm’s ability to assimilate and improve this decorative fabric.
It leverages the firm’s jacquard and functional-finish knowledge, has stable website promotion, and serves contract customers where flame retardancy is valued.
Its wool blend conflicts with the shift toward recyclable mono-materials, and limited promotion suggests weak early results that the firm cannot easily improve.

Although wool aligns with sustainability, the leno structure is outside the firm’s core upholstery and jacquard capabilities, and weak promotion indicates it cannot learn enough from early results to improve it.
The braided structure is newer but the product has dedicated website space, and the firm’s production partners and creative development provide the absorptive capacity to learn and improve it.
